detailed_rationale: [DATA] Authum Investment & Infrastructure (AIIL), promoted by the Dangi family (Sanjay/Alpana/Divy Dangi), runs a dual-engine model: an investment portfolio of ~Rs.15,592 cr (Q2 FY26) that is ~90%+ listed equities (large/midcap concentrated, per CRISIL), plus an NBFC/credit book built on distressed-asset acquisitions -- Reliance Commercial Finance (bought for Rs.1 cr, 2022) and Reliance Home Finance's business (Rs.3,351 cr, the largest NBFC resolution outside bankruptcy courts) -- now carrying >Rs.2,300 cr of loan assets (Sep-2025) on ~Rs.4,000 cr of fresh disbursements over 2 years. It layers on opportunistic IBC-route real-estate resolutions (NCLT approved Creatoz Builders/CBPL 16-Jul-2026; earlier AA Estates; but NCLT REJECTED the Vas Infrastructure resolution plan, Jul-2026). A 99.99%-shareholder-approved MOA amendment (postal ballot closed 27-Jun-2026) now permits portfolio management, AMC/mutual-fund sponsorship, ARC and infra-lending -- a real scope expansion beyond today's business. [DATA] FY26 (Mar-26) consolidated: revenue Rs.2,609 cr, net profit Rs.1,929 cr, EPS Rs.22.74 -- down sharply from FY25's Rs.4,580 cr revenue / Rs.4,241 cr PAT, because FY25 carried outsized one-off gains (Q4 FY25 alone booked Rs.1,763 cr PAT on just Rs.1,452 cr revenue -- profit exceeding revenue is the signature of fair-value/MTM gains flowing in below the revenue line). FY26 quarterly PAT was extremely lumpy (Q1 943 / Q2 767 / Q3 161 / Q4 58 cr), confirming earnings are gains-on-investment driven, not steady operating income. Q1 FY27 (out 20-Jul-2026) re-accelerated: revenue Rs.1,470 cr (+21% YoY), PAT Rs.1,108 cr (+17.5% YoY). Balance sheet is very strong: net worth Rs.16,670 cr (Jun-25), gearing 0.1x, CRAR 54.2% (Mar-25). Legacy lending-book asset quality: GNPA 10.5% including PTCs but NNPA just 0.9% (Jun-25) -- CRISIL confirms this NPA sits 'entirely from the acquired portfolio' and is fully provisioned, i.e. a capped legacy item, not fresh organic slippage. [DATA] At CMP ~Rs.555, AIIL trades at ~3.2x book value (Rs.173/share) and ~22.5x TTM P/E -- a striking premium-to-book for a vehicle that is mostly a listed-equity portfolio; Indian investment holdcos of this structure typically trade at a discount to NAV. CRISIL's own rating note (upgraded to A/Stable, Oct-2025) flags 'limited track record of profitably scaling the non-investment business' as the top weakness. [DATA/verified fresh] Promoter Sanjay Dangi (non-executive promoter-director, Dangi Group) was reported (Bombay HC filing, Jun-2024) as slated by CBI to be named an accused in the Rs.34,000-cr DHFL/Yes Bank scam chargesheet; the Special Court REFUSED to take cognisance of that chargesheet on 13-Mar-2025, ruling the cheating allegation had no basis -- a genuine de-risking event as of the most recent update found, though any CBI appeal status is unverified in this pass. Separately, whole-time director Divy Dangi was reported questioned by CBI regarding a Bank of Maharashtra fraud FIR tied to the pre-acquisition RCFL entity (a legacy, pre-2022-takeover matter). CFO Amit Kumar Jha resigned effective 1-Jun-2026 (company cites 'better career opportunities'); contemporaneous reporting notes the stock fell on the news -- an amber, not confirmed-red, governance flag.
recommendation_rationale: No quant score exists yet for AIIL, so per V1 default I hold rather than manufacture a Sell. The balance sheet is genuinely strong (0.1x gearing, 54% CRAR, and the legacy NNPA is fully provisioned at 0.9%), and Q1 FY27 momentum is positive, so there is no forced-sell case on fundamentals alone. But a ~3.2x price-to-book on what is substantially a listed-equity investment company, earnings dominated by lumpy MTM/recovery gains (FY26 PAT -55% YoY off a gains-heavy FY25 base), an unproven pivot into ARC/AMC/real-estate/infra-lending via the new MOA, and a promoter with real (if now court-rejected) scam-probe history are enough that I would not initiate or add here. I am flagging this honestly as a name the quant score may independently mark Sell once computed, without pre-empting that call myself.
summary: AIIL is a Dangi-family-promoted investment company (~Rs.15,600 cr portfolio, ~90%+ listed equities) that has built a distressed-asset NBFC/real-estate-resolution business atop the acquired Reliance Commercial Finance / Reliance Home Finance book, most recently adding the Creatoz Builders resolution (NCLT nod 16-Jul-2026) and a shareholder-approved MOA expansion into AMC/ARC/infra-lending. FY26 PAT fell to Rs.1,929 cr from FY25's gain-inflated Rs.4,241 cr, though Q1 FY27 (out 20-Jul-2026) rebounded to Rs.1,108 cr (+17.5% YoY); the balance sheet is very strong (0.1x gearing, 54% CRAR) and the legacy NPA book is fully provisioned (NNPA 0.9%), but the stock's ~3.2x price-to-book is rich for an investment vehicle with lumpy, gains-driven earnings, an unproven lending/ARC scale-up, and a promoter (Sanjay Dangi) with a recently court-rejected DHFL-scam chargesheet in his history.
positive_para: Balance sheet is fortress-like for the risk taken -- net worth Rs.16,670 cr, gearing just 0.1x, CRAR 54.2%, ample capacity to keep bargain-hunting distressed assets. The NBFC book built from the RCFL/RHFL resolutions (>Rs.2,300 cr loans, Sep-2025) is scaling with real disbursement volume (~Rs.4,000 cr over 2 years), and the legacy NPA overhang (GNPA 10.5% incl. PTCs) is fully provisioned down to a 0.9% net NPA -- a known, capped legacy problem, not fresh slippage. Q1 FY27 (revenue +21%, PAT +17.5% YoY) shows the model still compounding, and the newly NCLT-approved Creatoz Builders acquisition plus the just-passed MOA amendment (99.99% shareholder approval) give management fresh, board-sanctioned avenues to keep redeploying capital.
negative_para: Earnings are not a clean read -- FY26 PAT (Rs.1,929 cr) fell 55% off FY25's gains-inflated Rs.4,241 cr, and even within FY26 quarterly PAT swung from Rs.943 cr to Rs.58 cr; a P&L this dependent on investment fair-value gains and recovery income makes any single-year 'growth rate' or 'P/E' on this name inherently unstable. At ~3.2x book value the market is charging a premium multiple for what is, by asset composition, mostly a listed-equity portfolio -- CRISIL itself calls scaling the lending/ARC business 'undemonstrated,' and the MOA expansion into AMC/ARC/infra-lending is scope creep until proven. Promoter Sanjay Dangi was slated by CBI for the DHFL/Yes Bank chargesheet (Rs.34,000 cr scam); the special court rejected that chargesheet in Mar-2025, a genuine positive, but the episode plus whole-time director Divy Dangi being separately reported questioned by CBI on a Bank of Maharashtra fraud FIR (legacy RCFL matter) keep a governance shadow on the name. The CFO's June-2026 resignation (stock fell on the news) adds a fresh, unconfirmed amber flag.
reverse_dcf_judgment: Rich. At ~Rs.555 and ~3.2x book value / ~22.5x TTM P/E, the market is pricing AIIL well above what a plain investment-holding company (~90%+ listed-equity book) should typically fetch -- Indian holdcos of this structure usually trade at a discount to NAV, not a 3x+ premium. Justifying the premium requires AIIL to deliver simultaneously on several unproven fronts: profitably scale the young NBFC book, keep sourcing bargain IBC resolutions (Creatoz Builders is the newest win; Vas Infrastructure was just rejected by NCLT, showing this isn't a sure thing), and stand up the newly-permitted ARC/AMC/portfolio-management lines from scratch. The deliverable growth is real but choppy (FY26 PAT -55% YoY off a gains-heavy FY25 base, Q1 FY27 +17.5%); sustaining a 3x book premium on that track record is a stretch.
